lead: Official figures showed the economy grew 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, while the oil regulator said a new $300 helicopter levy did not apply to private offshore facilities. Former Bayelsa governor Timipre Sylva left the APC and the EFCC asked him to report for questioning. Gunmen abducted an APC council chairman in Kano, diphtheria spread in Plateau, and FIFA accepted the resignation of the NFF board.

items.h: Economy grows 4.43% in second quarter as GDP reaches N119.29trn
items.s: The National Bureau of Statistics said real GDP grew 4.43 per cent year on year in the second quarter of 2026, led by services while the real sector slowed sharply. The finance ministry said the figures keep Nigeria on course for its target of a $1 trillion economy by 2030.

items.h: Upstream regulator says $300 helicopter levy does not apply to private offshore sites
items.s: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission told federal agencies that no new fee affecting upstream operations should be introduced without consulting it, citing Section 25 of the Petroleum Industry Act. It said the $300 helicopter charge did not apply to private offshore facilities.

items.h: Timipre Sylva quits the APC and urges Nigerians to vote the party out
items.s: Former Bayelsa governor and ex-petroleum minister Timipre Sylva resigned from the All Progressives Congress and called on Nigerians to remove the party at the polls. The National Democratic Congress has been linked with his next move.

items.h: EFCC asks Sylva to come in for questioning over alleged $14.86m fraud
items.s: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission said former Bayelsa governor Timipre Sylva should make himself available for questioning. Its spokesman, Dele Oyewale, was responding to allegations Sylva made against the commission in his APC resignation letter.

items.h: Gunmen abduct APC chairman of Rogo council in Kano
items.s: Gunmen abducted Alhaji Abdullahi Fanka, the APC chairman of Rogo Local Government Area, from his hometown of Beli on Monday night. Residents said the attackers arrived around 10pm shooting sporadically before taking him away.

items.h: PDP national vice chairman Daniel Orbih dies at 64
items.s: Chief Daniel Osi Orbih, the Peoples Democratic Party's national vice chairman for the South South, died on 31 August 2026. FCT Minister Nyesom Wike described his death as a painful loss of a friend and political ally.

items.h: JAMB and WAEC set N4,000 fee to verify O'Level results
items.s: The Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board and the West African Examinations Council fixed a one-off N4,000 fee for verifying WASSCE and other O'Level results. Candidates seeking admission to tertiary institutions will have to verify their results under the new arrangement.

items.h: National ranking made compulsory for all universities, polytechnics and colleges of education
items.s: Education Minister Tunji Alausa said every university, polytechnic and college of education must now take part in the national tertiary ranking exercise. He announced it in Abuja at a meeting of the expanded ranking advisory committee.

items.h: FIFA accepts resignation of NFF president Gusau and the executive board
items.s: The Nigeria Football Federation said FIFA had accepted the resignations of president Ibrahim Gusau, general secretary Mohammed Sanusi and the executive committee, who quit under pressure over the national teams' repeated failures. The NFF separately dismissed as fake a letter claiming FIFA had queried government interference.

items.h: Supreme Council for Shariah urges rule of law in El-Rufai's detention
items.s: The Supreme Council for Shariah in Nigeria called on the authorities to follow the rule of law in the continued detention of former Kaduna governor Nasir El-Rufai. Its secretary-general, Nafiu Baba Ahmad, warned against political persecution.

items.h: Court stops regulator from shutting Dangote Refinery
items.s: A court restrained the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority from closing the Dangote Petroleum Refinery. A national polytechnic students' body urged both sides to settle their dispute through dialogue to avoid fuel supply disruptions.

items.h: Petrol reaches N1,350 a litre as Dangote and marketers' feud deepens
items.s: Daily Trust reported that the dispute between the Dangote refinery and marketers over petrol imports and pricing has pushed pump prices to about N1,350. The refinery is considering restricting supplies to major marketers that continue to import.

items.h: Military rescues 21 kidnap victims, including 15 NYSC members, in Kogi forest
items.s: Security forces rescued corps members abducted in Kogi State on 26 August as they travelled to Abuja from the Bayelsa orientation camp, along with other kidnap victims. The NYSC commended the agencies involved.

items.h: Mother and four children die as building partly collapses in Ilorin
items.s: A section of a three-storey building collapsed on a family at 41 Popo Giwa Street, Ilorin, on Tuesday morning, killing a mother and four of her children. Eight family members were trapped under the rubble.

items.h: Diphtheria outbreak kills 15 in Jos North
items.s: Local authorities said at least 15 people have died and more than 100 are suspected to be infected with diphtheria in communities across Jos North, Plateau State. They warned that more cases are likely.

items.h: Katsina health workers announce seven-day warning strike amid diphtheria outbreak
items.s: Healthcare workers in Katsina State declared a seven-day warning strike from 8 September and threatened an indefinite one if their demands are not met. The state is battling a worsening diphtheria outbreak.

items.h: Customs seizes 204 rifles in container from Turkey
items.s: The Tin Can Island command of the Nigeria Customs Service intercepted 204 pump-action rifles and firearm parts concealed in a 20-foot container imported from Turkey. It came three weeks after the same command seized 399 rifles.

items.h: Court adjourns Atiku's suit on Tinubu's eligibility to 28 September
items.s: The Federal High Court in Abuja adjourned former Vice President Atiku Abubakar's suit seeking to disqualify President Tinubu and the APC from the 2027 election after a dispute over service of court papers. The case was moved to 28 September.

items.h: Court voids APC Zamfara North senatorial primary and orders fresh poll
items.s: A Federal High Court in Gusau nullified the APC primary held on 19 May 2026 for the Zamfara North senatorial seat and ordered a new one. Four aspirants had contested the primary.

items.h: Turaki-led PDP faction backs G-100 plan for an opposition coalition
items.s: The Tanimu Turaki faction of the PDP endorsed the effort by 100 opposition figures, known as the G-100, to build a single platform against the APC in 2027. It said the opposition needed to unite.

items.h: Remi Tinubu asks Nigerians to back the President's re-election
items.s: First Lady Oluremi Tinubu urged APC members and Nigerians to support President Tinubu's re-election in 2027. She spoke in Ibadan at the launch of the Tinubu Torch Bearer Movement.

items.h: Donald Duke says Tinubu's tenure has exposed the APC's weaknesses
items.s: Donald Duke, presidential candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party, criticised the governing party and weighed in on the debate between President Tinubu and former Vice President Atiku Abubakar.

items.h: Shettima says Nigeria will not tolerate xenophobic attacks on its citizens
items.s: Vice President Kashim Shettima said Nigeria will no longer accept the mistreatment of its citizens abroad and called on South Africans to rethink xenophobic attacks. He spoke in Luanda after representing President Tinubu at an extraordinary regional summit.

items.h: New ECOWAS Commission president calls for closer ties with Sahel states
items.s: General Birame Diop, the new president of the ECOWAS Commission, said the bloc must strengthen its unity and deepen engagement with the Alliance of Sahel States. He spoke at his handover ceremony in Abuja.

items.h: EFCC says it recovered N1.23trn and secured 10,872 convictions in 34 months
items.s: EFCC chairman Ola Olukoyede said the commission recovered more than N1.23 trillion and $684.48 million in proceeds of crime between October 2023 and June 2026. He presented the figures in his three-year stewardship report in Abuja.

items.h: APM tells Tinubu to quit 2027 race over US drug case
items.s: The Allied Peoples Movement called on President Tinubu to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race, citing allegations it said were before a United States court. The party said Nigeria needed a president free of such allegations.

items.h: Cleric asks two Abia North candidates to step down for Orji Kalu
items.s: A Baptist cleric, Rev. Samson Okoro Elekwa, urged the Labour Party and NDC candidates for the Abia North Senate seat to withdraw in favour of the incumbent, Senator Orji Uzor Kalu of the APC.

items.h: Police arrest five in Bauchi over suspected human eyes
items.s: Police at Zone 12 headquarters in Bauchi arrested five suspects allegedly found with two suspected human eyes and other items linked to money rituals.

items.h: UBTH says its cancer centre is fully operational
items.s: The University of Benin Teaching Hospital said its cancer centre is now fully running, including radiotherapy for patients who cannot pay. The chief medical director spoke as the hospital received a new ambulance from the Federal Government.

items.h: Police probe senator, Borno commissioner and Kuje council chair over inciting remarks
items.s: The police high command said it is investigating alleged inciting comments by Osun East Senator Francis Fadahunsi, Borno youth and sports commissioner Sainna Buba and Kuje Area Council chairman Danjuma Shekwolo ahead of 2027.

items.h: Troops kill two terrorist commanders in Katsina
items.s: Soldiers of Operation Fansan Yamma killed two senior commanders of a group led by Kachalla Muhammadu Filani in Matazu Local Government Area during an intelligence-led operation, Daily Trust reported.

items.h: Bandits attack 17 villages in Faskari
items.s: A Faskari council report said bandits raided at least 17 villages in the Katsina local government area, killing and kidnapping residents. Many families have left their homes in fear.

items.h: Military explains withdrawal of 200 US troops from Nigeria
items.s: The Defence Headquarters said the reported withdrawal of United States troops did not mean security cooperation between the two countries had broken down. Its spokesman, Samaila Uba, spoke at a briefing in Abuja.

items.h: More than 12 state universities shut as zero-strike policy is tested
items.s: BusinessDay reported that at least 12 state-owned universities have shut down, putting the Federal Government's zero-strike policy to the test.

items.h: INEC denies altering NDC candidate list
items.s: The Independent National Electoral Commission rejected claims by the Nigeria Democratic Congress that its officials changed the party's 2027 candidate list. INEC said it has no power to nominate or substitute any party's candidates.

items.h: ADC faction condemns Atiku's use of party name in foreign suit against Tinubu
items.s: The board of trustees and working committee of an ADC faction accused former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, the party's 2027 presidential candidate, of using its name and logo without authorisation.

items.h: Atiku says a minimum wage now buys about 40 litres of petrol
items.s: Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar criticised the Tinubu administration's economic policies, saying the price of petrol means a worker's monthly minimum wage can be used up on about 40 litres.

items.h: ADC rejects Presidency's N19.1trn cost estimate for fuel subsidy
items.s: The African Democratic Congress rejected the Presidency's claim that restoring the petrol subsidy to hold pump prices near N600 would cost N19.1 trillion a year, saying Nigerians are too poor to go without support.

items.h: Power minister says energy security now depends on grid resilience
items.s: Power Minister Joseph Tegbe said energy security is no longer only about oil and gas reserves but about resilient grids, critical minerals and the institutions that keep electricity flowing.

items.h: Money supply rises to N138.78trn in July despite tight policy
items.s: Nigeria's broad money supply rose to N138.78 trillion in July 2026, up 16 per cent from a year earlier, according to Central Bank of Nigeria data reported by Nairametrics.

items.h: FG starts TV audience measurement in Lagos with free data for homes
items.s: The Federal Government began the first phase of a national television audience measurement system in Lagos. Selected households will receive 36GB of data a month for taking part.

items.h: WIOCC raises $300m to expand Africa's digital infrastructure
items.s: Digital infrastructure firm WIOCC Group secured a combined $300 million from the Africa Finance Corporation and Vision International Investment Company to expand across the continent.

items.h: NSIA Insurance leaves life business and transfers portfolio to CHI Life
items.s: NSIA Insurance said it will operate only as a non-life insurer after transferring its life insurance portfolio to CHI Life Assurance.

items.h: Kano police arrest 244 suspects in August
items.s: The Kano State Police Command said it arrested 244 suspects and recovered pistols, ammunition and drugs during operations in August.

items.h: NDLEA arrests 140 and seizes 816kg of drugs in Kaduna
items.s: The Kaduna command of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency arrested 140 suspected drug offenders and seized 816.5kg of assorted drugs.

items.h: FCT Miyetti Allah chairman dies in road crash
items.s: Alhaji Ardo Wokili Madugu, chairman of the FCT chapter of the Miyetti Allah Cattle Breeders Association, died in a crash on the Lambata-Izom road in Niger State.

items.h: Ebonyi governor tells new council chairmen to deliver for APC or risk removal
items.s: Governor Francis Nwifuru warned the 13 newly sworn-in local government chairmen in Ebonyi that they risk losing their posts if they fail to deliver their areas to the APC in 2027.

items.h: Falconets play final friendly against Korea before U20 World Cup
items.s: Acting NFF general secretary Emmanuel Ikpeme urged Nigeria's U20 women's team to keep a winning mentality in their last friendly against the Republic of Korea before the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup.

items.h: Organisers seek support for maiden National Intermediate Games in Lagos
items.s: The organising committee of the first National Intermediate Games, Eko 2026, appealed for media support. The games run in Lagos from 1 to 15 October with more than 15,000 athletes expected.

items.h: Funke Akindele unveils first images from new film The Four
items.s: Filmmaker Funke Akindele released the first images from The Four: No One Fights Alone, which opens in cinemas on 11 December 2026.
